messages:
elaine: FYI ran a focused perf sweep after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. small-chat prompts (~<80 tokens) on the small A100 fleet show p50 decode up ~30ms and p95 spikes up to 400ms. digging in now.
aj: ouch. is this decode-only or prefill too?
elaine: initial look points at increased kernel arbitration + more frequent kernel handoffs during decode. prefill grouping got more aggressive so prefill batches sometimes win the kernel pipeline right as decodes arrive. KV priming also seems to trigger more often because prefill windows are longer.
sam: can you paste the profiler top-lines?
elaine: paste from the smoke run: 
```nprofile: kernel_arbitrate_and_handoff: 58%
profile: kv_prime: 20% (cold->warm transitions up)
profile: stream_serialization: 12%
profile: scheduling_idle_wait: 10%
note: decode latency variance temporally aligns with kernel handoff bursts
```
priya: that smells like queue-level interference. when prefill batches are coalesced they occupy kernel scheduling and small decode batches get parked.
aj: quick mitigation ideas: soft-separate prefill/decode admission; tiny decode token budget to keep gen short; "kernel wave" limiter to cap concurrent handoffs; lazy KV prime threshold to avoid unnecessary priming.
elaine: I prototyped a runtime config toggle to exercise those knobs. example config we used: 
```n# runtime tuning (canary)
batching.phase_separation: soft
batching.token_budget.prefill: 128
batching.token_budget.decode: 12
batching.kernel_wave.limit: 5
prefill.kv.lazy_prime_min_hit_pred: 0.25  # prime only if predicted hit >= 25%
```
sam: i like it. would also add admission backpressure for prefill when decode depth is nontrivial.
priya: plus a kernel selector hint: prefer low-latency kernel variants for stage==decode && batch_size<=8, even if throughput slightly worse. that reduces p95.
aj: will add a decode-affinity hint to the selector branch (prefer kernel-B for small decode batches).
elaine: i also added a prefill admission probability that ramps down if decode_queue_len > threshold. pseudocode: 
```nif decode_queue_len > 10: prefill_admit_prob = 0.2
else: prefill_admit_prob = 1.0
```
sam: good. important that separation is "soft" so we don't accidentally tank utilization on busy models.
dev-bot: perf-smoke job #789 finished 61; 10k requests per cohort.
elaine: plan: A/B canary where group A has phase_separation + token budgets + kernel_wave; group B control. collect decode_p50/p95, kv_hit_rate, kernel_handoff_gauge over 8-12h.
priya: add metrics: kernel_handoff_count, kernel_handoff_time, kv_prime_rate, prefill_admit_rate. also surface per-route breakdown in the console so product/SRE can sanity-check by model.
aj: i'll land selector hint behind feature flag and wire the config toggles.
ops: note: Dedicated pools will need a separate rollout + ops-runbook update.
elaine: acknowledged, i'll coordinate with ops once the canary metrics look healthy.
sam: one more test: run with lazy_prime_threshold=0.0 (no priming) vs 0.25 to measure KV warmup impact on coast and latency.
elaine: yep will run both and post charts. if decode p95 is better and throughput loss is within 3% we'll promote. will also include a short writeup. :thumbsup:
